Okay, this update looks quite interesting. ChatGPT's latest update adds a new Mac integration feature: it can handle conversations in Apple's Messages app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now includes an Apple Messages plugin

The new Apple Messages plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat history on Mac, as well as compose and send messages. OpenAI says the feature is available on all plans of the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, and also supports ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Since the feature involves access permissions, it raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that in the default setting, sending actions still require user confirmation. Users should think carefully before granting continuous authorisation. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the relevant risks, how to revoke authorisation, and a known issue involving tasks that disable confirmation prompts.

For now, this feature is only available on Macs with Apple silicon; Intel models are not currently supported.

If you ask ChatGPT to send a message on your behalf, it will prompt you to confirm before sending. Users can also choose to skip the confirmation step in individual conversations.

Looking for this new feature in ChatGPT? This link should take you directly to the Messages plugin page for ChatGPT on Mac.

Site co-editing, shared thread snapshots, and more

Although the Messages plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also includes several other improvements. For example, pinned conversations now stay in sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, so users can access important conversations on Mac and iPhone at any time.

ChatGPT now also lets users share read-only snapshots of local Codex threads. These snapshots do not update as the original thread changes.

Links created from personal accounts can be viewed by anyone with the URL, while workspace links are only accessible to members of that workspace. OpenAI says Codex masks known sensitive formats, but still reminds users to review snapshot content, as sensitive information may still remain.

In addition, Site owners can invite active members within the same workspace to co-edit collaborative Sites. Editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes after the owner has completed the initial publication. Owners retain control over access, settings, analytics, and version restoration.

Some Site owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, with old addresses automatically redirecting to the new ones.

Finally, the Computer History feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK. This is an optional feature that requires Memories to be enabled and is off by default.

You can read the full release notes for this update here.
